Need to search first.I wasn't able to write any notes on Jeremiah 19. None of the research went through, so I have no sourced content to give you. Your rule is that every point has to come from a page I actually read, with its URL, so I've written nothing from memory.

**What happened:**
- **First attempt:** I tried to open six pages directly: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, and the NET Bible notes. All six were refused because the tool only opens addresses that have already turned up in a search.
- **Second attempt:** I ran ten searches covering those commentaries plus Topheth/Ben-hinnom, Jeremiah 19:5 and the Valley of Hinnom. That call was blocked because I'd used up my tool limit for this turn, and a test call afterwards was blocked too. I didn't get any search results back.

**To finish this, I'll need a new turn (just reply "continue").** I'll start by searching so the pages can be opened, then read:
1. **The main reading:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub or StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon, Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God, Grace to You, and the Lutheran sites (LCMS, 1517). Verse 5 ("nor did it even enter My mind") is probably the likeliest place for a real disagreement, since it touches on God's foreknowledge. I'd only report a difference if the sources actually show one.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey on Topheth and Hinnom/Gehenna (vv. 2, 6, 11–13), and Catholic and Orthodox readings from New Advent, Catholic.com and OCA. I'd cover modern popular teaching such as prosperity or word-of-faith only if those sites discuss this chapter.

If you'd like, I could do just one of these parts per turn so each batch fits within the limit.
